rows.why: S1 covers four things, and three items each answer part of it: item 1 (row order), item 8 (header) and item 9 (BOM and CRLF on every row). Item 9 is the closest because it settles two of the four clauses. The run shows the BOM at the start and CRLF after every row, the last one included. Items 1 and 8 also agree: the header is 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', and rows are sorted by creation time, then id.

No item asks how the status is shown to readers. Item 4 is only about which input statuses are valid. The closest is item 10, which asks how the creation time is formatted. S2 wants the UTC date only, as YYYY-MM-DD, but the run wrote '2024-01-01T10:20:30.456Z'. The run for item 4 also shows status written raw ('open'), not 'Open'.
An empty list produced just the BOM and the header row, ending in CRLF, which is what S3 expects.

Item 12 asks how fields with separators are escaped. The run shows a comma, quote and newline being quoted with the quote doubled, and '@cmd' written without quotes. But S4 also wants quoting when a title starts or ends with a space. Neither 'quotes per RFC 4180' nor the run says what happens then, so I can't tell.
Item 12 also asks whether formula prefixes are neutralized. The pick says they are not, and the run shows '=SUM(...)' and '@cmd' written without the leading single quote that S5 requires.

Item 3 asks what happens with bad data: unknown status, bad counts, filled over openings, or an invalid date. It throws an Error that names the id ('Requisition REQ-9: unknown status "bogus"'), which matches S6.
